objects_domains_binders.expectation: All scalars and matrices are real; vectors are finite-dimensional Euclidean vectors with the standard dot product and Euclidean norm. Transpose means real matrix transpose; <x,y>=x^T y.
S2 has integer d>=1, real κ>=1, A in R^(d×d), A=A^T, I_d≼A≼κ I_d. The selected constructed A must genuinely instantiate this class if named an S2 input.

f_A is the scalar function x↦(1/2)x^T A x on all R^d, not a new unconstrained potential. FO_A(x) is the ordered pair (f_A(x),∇f_A(x)); for symmetric A the actual gradient is Ax. It is an exact response, with no noise or normalization constant in f_A.

Source fixes κ>=4, integer 3<=n<=d, k=floor(d/n); hence k>=1, kn<=d, r=d-kn with 0<=r<n. Source also discusses n=2T+1 when T>=1 and 2T+1<=d; this T-choice is downstream context rather than an identity premise. A theorem over broader algebraic parameters must explicitly specialize back to this source family.

Universally quantify O=(O_1,...,O_k)∈O(n)^k; O_j are real n×n orthogonal matrices. A_Oj=((κ+1)/2)I_n-((κ-1)/4)(O_j+O_j^T). A_boldO is the d×d block diagonal matrix diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_r). No determinant sign, prior, independence or expectation is needed in these pointwise identities.

For every x∈R^d write x=(x_1,...,x_k,z), each x_j∈R^n and z∈R^r, using the same fixed ordered block decomposition as S3.E5. It is a Euclidean identification covering all d coordinates and preserving inner products. When r=0 the identity block and z terms are omitted; an implementation with a zero-dimensional residual must identify it with this source convention. The z here is a fixed coordinate component, not the normalized residual observation z in B.2/B.3.

j∈{1,...,k}, v∈R^n, τ exactly one of {f,i}; primitive(j,v,f)=O_j v, primitive(j,v,i)=O_j^T v. Inverse is the transpose response because O_j is orthogonal, not a matrix inverse operation with a failure/default branch.

For every family tuple and every x, row Ex33 additionally ranges over every legal block j. Formula variables are fixed pointwise; no random draw, history, seed, expectation, conditional law, or query budget occurs in these equations.

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: A_Oj and A_boldO are symmetric. Source explicitly states symmetry in B.3; derivation uses transpose of sum, scalar matrices and (O^T)^T=O.
necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.classification: source structural fact requiring proof in target

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: Orthogonality gives ||Ov||=||v||; Cauchy–Schwarz bounds |<v,Ov>|<=||v||²; inserting S3.E4 yields ||v||²<=v^T A_O v<=κ||v||². Block decomposition and κ>=1 extend these bounds over the identity residual, proving A_boldO∈A_dκ.
necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.classification: necessary model admission ancestry, not an assumption replacing the construction

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: The source writes a genuine mathematical gradient. It does not spell out a Fréchet/coordinate differentiation proof for the quadratic. A target must supply standard finite-dimensional calculus and derivative existence, rather than introducing differentiability as a new public premise. For symmetric A, Df(x)[h]=(1/2)(h^T Ax+x^T Ah)=<Ax,h>.
necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.classification: omitted standard calculus proof obligation; not a public source assumption

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: A theorem only about the value of a totalized gradient operator can hold through a default when differentiability is unestablished. Source fidelity requires actual derivative existence for the concrete potential at every x and identification of its gradient with the reconstructed vector. Merely defining the oracle gradient field to be Ax does not prove this calculus claim.
necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.classification: formalization audit requirement inferred from source semantics; not a source premise

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: Supply the concrete finite coordinate partition/linear isometry between R^d and (R^n)^k×R^r, its inverse, block action and norm/inner-product decomposition, including r=0. Source uses this standard convention without a named theorem. An arbitrary block operator or bespoke product inner product is not automatically the concrete S3.E5 real matrix model.
necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.classification: omitted standard coordinate proof obligation; not a public source assumption

necessary_regularities_and_missing_stand.requirement: The value, gradient and primitive responses must all refer to the same O tuple and the same concrete f_A. An unconstrained queried value/gradient field or theorem taking the desired identities as hypotheses does not independently reconstruct the source FO response.
